blocks.heading: Three Court Decisions in Plain Words

items.text: These rulings do not change a recruiter's published medical standard.
Note The Court adopted the view of a seven-member committee that colour grading has no real link to an editor's role, because colourists handle colour work.
Routes are ordered by how far proof of skill can lift income.
The work is logic, text and numbers on a screen, and the proof is a working project.
Who pays you Hiring managers at tech and analytics firms; later, clients who buy a finished project.

blocks.heading: Get a Proper Test Before You Choose
rows: School or camp screening
A quick plate or app check, often done once in a school health camp.
A hint only. It does not tell you the type, the degree or what a recruiter's board will decide.
Ishihara plates
Armed forces boards use it at the first stage, and the railway Station Master proforma lists it with the required result 'Normal'.
The test most recruiters name first, so ask for a result on paper from a doctor.
Lantern test
You name coloured signal lights at a set distance. A paper on Indian Air Force standards describes the Martin Lantern for pilot grading.
Matters for flying and signalling roles. Recruiters set their own pass mark.
Anomaloscope
A matching test that grades how strong the deficiency is. The armed forces colour perception guidelines, as quoted by the Delhi High Court, use it with Ishihara at appeal and review boards.
Where a case reaches a review board, this is the harder check. Ask an eye specialist whether it is available near you.

blocks.heading: Who Tests Colour Vision
rows: Armed forces (Army, Navy, Air Force)
Colour perception is assessed with Ishihara at the first medical board, and at the appellate and review boards Army, Navy and Air Force candidates are tested with both Ishihara and the anomaloscope.

Read the exact medical standard in the notice for your entry (NDA, CDS, technical entry) before you pay for coaching. The court sent one candidate back for a fresh review board because the test was not done as the guidelines say.
Pilots

A paper in the Indian Journal of Aerospace Medicine, quoting the Air Force manual IAP 4303, gives the military standard as no errors on the first 25 of 38 Ishihara plates, plus a lantern test at 6 m. For the civil pilot licence it describes a separate lantern or Ishihara standard, with failure graded unfit.
Civil flying medicals are set by the aviation regulator (DGCA), whose own current document we did not read. Check it before you pay for flying school.
Indian Railways
The RRB proforma in notice CEN 05/2024, for the Station Master post (medical category A-2), says colour vision is tested with the Ishihara test and the required result is 'Normal'.
Each railway post has its own medical category. Read the category for the post in the current notice.
Merchant navy
A merchant navy training guide reports that any colour blindness is not permitted in any department, with the Ishihara chart recommended. It does not cite the shipping regulator's own document.
Treat this as a warning, not a rule. Confirm with the DG Shipping medical standard and the training institute before you apply.
Electrical and power companies
In the TANGEDCO case, the employer admitted it had no norm fixing colour vision as an eligibility condition for Assistant Engineer. Rules differ by employer and post.
Ask the recruiting body in writing whether colour vision is a stated condition, and keep the reply.
Medicine

After a Supreme Court order in 2017, an expert committee concluded that colour vision deficiency 'is not and should not be an absolute bar in the medical profession'. The Medical Council said in 2017 that it would lift its bar.
That is 2017 reporting. Check the current National Medical Commission rules for your course.

blocks.heading: Work Out Your Own Colour Load
rows: Reading colour-coded charts and dashboards
Medium. Legends that rely on red versus green are the problem.
Ask for patterns, labels or numbers beside colours. In your own work, use labelled series and accessible palettes.
Choosing and matching colours
High for design and fashion work.
Work from colour codes, a contrast checker and a colleague for final colour sign-off. Make colour decisions with names and numbers.
Wiring and cables
High where many wires look alike.
Labels, tags and a continuity tester. Raise this with the employer before you accept, as the TANGEDCO case shows how it can become a dispute.
Signals and lights
High in rail, sea and air roles.
These roles have formal tests. No workaround is allowed, so plan another route.
Medical images, rashes, stains
Depends on the specialty.
Ask the course and the regulator what they require. Do not assume.
Writing, analysis, coding, accounts, teaching
Low.
Little or none. Spend your effort here if you want the widest choice.

blocks.heading: Routes with a Medical Entry Requirement
rows: Armed forces and railways
A written exam rank, then call-up for selection.
The medical board, where colour vision is tested and can end the process even after a good rank.
Pilot training
Entry tests and a medical for the licence you want.
A flying school fee paid before some people learn they cannot clear the colour standard. Check the medical first.
Medicine
A national entrance exam rank for a limited number of seats.
Postgraduate seat competition and the specialty choice, where colour cues can matter.

blocks.heading: Tools and AI for Colour-Blind Professionals

items.text: Browser developer tools can simulate colour blindness, so you can check your own designs.
Contrast checkers test text and background pairs against accessibility guidelines.
Phone apps name colours through the camera for everyday choices.
AI assistants can describe a chart or suggest an accessible palette.
